Well, wouldn't it be cool?

A 3rd person open world game where you play as a fascist future cop. We've got a lot of open world city games set in the present day, but none set in an imaginative dystopian future city. I would buy a game that lets you cruise around a dystopian nightmare of a city playing as one of its most powerful and dangerous inhabitants. You'd get to be a highway patrolman, a detective, a SWAT officer, etc.

What better universe than Judge Dredd, and what better city than Megacity 1?

The comics have a wealth of material to pull missions and story from, a lot of the storylines are bizarre and really imaginative. The devs could have a lot of fun exploring the issues around totalitarianism and fascism, Dredd is both a likeable character yet totally unrelatable and brutal. There are a lot of other interesting characters in the universe who could appear in side quests and bonus missions. And people loved the movie.

I think the time is ripe for a futuristic open world city game, it's only a matter of time before one is made, why not make it about Dredd?

As you can probably imagine, they are brutal, fascist hardasses who hand out harsh sentences and frequently kill people. The ironic and terrible thing is, they're a far preferable alternative to the nightmarish gang members, mutants, zombies, vampires, and other scum who populate megacity 1.

I never understood whats wrong with a vote brigade. If users dont like a comment and downvote it all together, than whats the problem?

Like drama subs, like SRD, where you see a post being called out for being le problematic, and you vote with yur beliefs, because you want to spread the word, fight the good fight, etc. This behaviour allows ideology brigade subs to exist and encourages them. Thats whats wrong with them, even if i also like to downvote the villain in the drama linked in some internet points pile on, i think everyone gets the impulse, its not too bad a behaviour, but it can create circlejerks and that makes discussion less free.
Yes I understand why vote brigades are bad, but I think they theres no way to control the votes of users, without censoring them

Maybe mods should have the ability to protect threads. Vote brigading is only an issue with downvoting, nobody has a problem with upvotes. So when a mod notices a vote brigade it sets the thread to protected. This disables the downvote button in that thread, and maybe allow only subscribers to comment

One of the problems with votes on reddit is how they weight the comment/post. If something is downvoted you say "i dont want this in the discussion" you try to do your part to censor it, remove it from the average persons view.

If you allowed voting to be free, but removed the vote weighting, only weighted by timestamp, no censorship of views happens, and discussion is more free. Brigades can be OK, if they have no power to weight the discussion their way.

In the same way as downvote brigades police one slant of a circlejerk, so would a mod cleansing "brigading", if it wasn't brigading. Its too easy for the mod to use as they see fit whenever the subs own circlejerk is under attack.

Brigades are easy to see with both upvotes and downvotes visible, unlike reddit, where they do seem to shape the discussion more since the visible ups/downs was removed. Also, can you imagine the whining it will bring out, everyone who gets downvoted will be bitchin at the mods.
